title: Main task screen
question: Compare the screen directions. All use named lists, rich task details, quick-add, and automatic sync with details on demand. The sketches show synthetic example tasks.

options.label: Margin notes
options.thesis: A clear task list with a consistent metadata margin and an adjacent task editor.
options.viewport: Lists at left, active tasks and quick-add in the middle, selected task details at right; due date and priority form a readable margin.
options.risk: Aligned metadata needs careful collapsing on narrow screens.

raised.raise: Show local-save and GitHub-sync checkpoints separately, with plain-language labels.
Keep each list’s identity consistent in navigation and task details.
Selection, priority, and sync states each have a distinct named meaning.
Give each task property one authoritative editing location.
Preserve the same readable type scale and alignment for long titles and dense metadata.

options.label: Wayfinder
options.thesis: Fast project switching, readable task rows, and a small two-stage sync indicator.
options.viewport: Named lists anchor a green rail, a broad task list leads, and details open alongside; a two-checkpoint indicator separates saved here from GitHub.
options.risk: An effective, familiar task-manager arrangement; less distinctive than the other directions.

options.label: After hours
options.thesis: A compact dark workspace keeps rich task details legible without a full-screen editor.
options.viewport: Lists at left, compact task rows centrally, and a persistent editor on the right; Git details appear only when requested.
options.case: Competitive on product clarity at high information density; the darker working scene is a preference still to confirm.
options.risk: Small low-contrast metadata would undermine readability; avoid a terminal costume.

options.label: Midnight transit diagram
options.thesis: A dark task workspace with an explicit local-to-GitHub sync trail.
options.viewport: Standard lists, task rows and a detail panel, with a compact sync trail.
options.case: Neither a stronger personal-task fit nor clearer metadata than Margin notes; the multi-ink vocabulary adds decoding.
options.kept: Separate local and remote persistence checkpoints.
options.risk: A route diagram can make a small sync status too prominent.

options.label: Character catalog
options.thesis: Consistent list identities make projects easy to recognize.
options.viewport: Standard task rows and editor, with softly tinted project markers.
options.case: No stronger audience identification or task clarity; portraits and ranked rosters have no job in this brief.
options.kept: Consistent list identity across navigation and details.
options.risk: Character decoration would compete with task content.

options.label: Orienteering map
options.thesis: A crisp task list uses a strict visual vocabulary for selection and state.
options.viewport: Standard lists and task editor with a clear selected-task marker.
options.case: The map vocabulary adds no personal-task identification or clarity once controls remain familiar.
options.kept: Selection and semantic status must remain distinct.
options.risk: A course or map metaphor would invent a workflow.

options.label: Factory catalog sleeve
options.thesis: Each task and property has one clear place.
options.viewport: Standard task list and details with deliberately reduced duplicate controls.
options.case: Encoded titles and vast empty space reduce task clarity and audience fit; keeping ordinary labels removes their premise.
options.kept: Each property has one authoritative editing location.
options.risk: Coded labels would obscure the work.

options.label: Type specimen
options.thesis: A precise type system keeps the task content easy to scan.
options.viewport: Ordinary task rows and a detail editor with rigorous type hierarchy.
options.case: Display scale and variable-axis interaction serve neither this user’s task nor its clarity.
options.kept: Test long titles and dense metadata as carefully as short content.
options.risk: Oversized typography would consume working space.

canonCard.label: Familiar task manager
canonCard.thesis: The conventional task-manager layout, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: Lists at left, task list in the middle and details on the right, with compact sync status.
canonCard.risk: Intentionally close to familiar task apps.
